threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it Dalston Lane instead of the actual Dalston Junction—everyone knows the real train's just a hop from the market.
Last night on the 196, a guy serenaded the whole bus with an off-key version of 'Wonderwall' while the rest just stared at their phones. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The morning I stepped into the bakery on Weserstraße and heard three different languages while picking up my Brötchen. That's when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find kebab shops open at 3 AM, serving both drunk locals and night owls. The late-night grill culture is unmatched.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their reaction to the BART delays—while newcomers complain online, we just shrug and keep walking to the next taco spot.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling in the back of the 38 while a woman in a wheelchair was singing opera. It was a wild mix of talent and chaos on a Tuesday morning.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is just a ‘hip’ area. But locals know the best cafes are the ones where the barista still remembers your name.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They always order a 'café con leche' and then look confused when it doesn’t come with a smile. Local etiquette is a whole different cup of coffee.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the bus driver calls out stops. Locals have that down to a fine art — just nod and know your destination.
Caught the 77 last night; a guy was tap dancing in the aisle while singing 90s R&B. Only in Brixton can the bus ride feel like a show.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Sitting at the café, I spotted a guy serenading a pigeon with a ukulele while a toddler danced beside him. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find kebab shops with vegan döner that taste just as good as the real thing. It’s a culinary revolution on every corner.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they navigate the BART delays with a resigned sigh and know to avoid the Civic Center entrance after a loud bang.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in the Tenderloin teaching his dog to press the Muni button with its nose. Meanwhile, the bus was 20 minutes late. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think we all love vermut on the terraces, but locals prefer a pint at the bar during the week. It’s about the vibe, not just the drinks.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by how they still carry a map and stare at it like it's a treasure map, while locals just keep walking with their phones out.
